;

; units in height and width, initially mapped
;
;   x0 = -192 * 1024 = -2.0        320 px * 1024 = 5.0     -> re in [-2.0,  3.0]
;   y0 = -100 * 1024 = -1.5625     200 px * 1024 = 3.125   -> im in [-1.5625, 1.5625]
;
; which covers the standard (-2, 0.5) x (-1.5, 1.5) region.  Zoom halves or
; doubles the per-pixel step about the centre of the screen, so the reachable
; range is BLOCK = 1024 down to 1, a 1024x magnification, at which point one
; pixel is one Q16.16 ulp and the fixed-point grid is exhausted.
;
; Products are formed with the one-operand IMUL (EDX:EAX = EAX * r/m32) and
; renormalised with SHRD, so each multiply is exact to 64 bits before the
; shift. At the top of the loop the escape test guarantees |z| < 2,
; but z' = z^2 + c can reach |z'| ~ 7.25 before the tst. But 7.25 * 65536
; squared is 2.3e11, well past 32 bits but comfortably inside 64.

ORG 0x7C00

H       equ 200
SH      equ 16                  ; fixed point fraction bits
BLOCK   equ 1024                ; widest-zoom step, Q16.16 units per pixel

content.text:
`esi`/`ebp` (c.re/c.im) — inside `.mandel` they're each touched only once per pass (the final `add ebx, esi` / `add eax, ebp`), whereas `zr2`/`zi2` are hit far more: two stores plus three reloads (`add eax,[zr2]`, `mov ebx,[zr2]`, `sub ebx,[zi2]`) per iteration.

Move c.re/c.im into a pair of memory locals set once per pixel (outside `.mandel`, alongside `sp, MAXIT`), and let `esi`/`ebp` hold `zr2`/`zi2` directly instead. That trades 5 memory accesses/iteration for 2, and `zr2`/`zi2` — the values actually being read and rewritten every pass — get to live in registers instead of the values that barely move.

; pixel is one Q16.16 ulp and the fixed-point grid is exhausted.

; renormalised with SHRD, so multiply is 64 bits before the
; shift. At the top of the loop the escape test guarantees |z| < 2,

ORG 0x7C00

H       equ 200
SH      equ 16                  ; fixed point fraction bits
BLOCK   equ 1024                ; widest-zoom step, Q16.16 units per pixel

content.text:
Found it — using `sp` as a loop counter without disabling interrupts. Nothing in the render loop stops the PIT timer tick (~18.2 Hz) from firing an `int 0x08`, which pushes `flags:cs:ip` onto whatever `ss:sp` currently is. Since `sp` is the iteration counter (1–128) during `.mandel`, those pushes land at physical addresses 0–~250 — squarely inside the interrupt vector table — smashing vectors 0–32 (including the timer's own vector, INT 0x08) every tick. Eventually a corrupted vector sends the CPU somewhere garbage and the render just stops partway, leaving the untouched rows black — exactly what the screenshot shows.

Fix: `cli` before the render loop, `sti` before the blocking keyboard wait (it needs IRQ1 to actually fill the buffer).
